derivation: Machine-extracted from Zoho ERP official OpenAPI bundle openapi-all.zip (SHA256 E95A0399...C447F8), downloaded 2026-08-05 from https://www.zoho.com/erp/api/v3/openapi-all.zip. Vendor-authoritative; supersedes page-scraped claims where they conflict.

findings.title: The ERP API is NOT uniformly /erp/v3 — 14 of 78 modules are served from /erp/v1
findings.impact: The connection profile cannot hold a single API base path. Base URL must be resolved per module, and the API Version field in the connection-profile master must be per-module, not per-connection.

findings.title: Purchase Request does not exist anywhere in the official ERP API specification
findings.impact: Mechanically proven clean negative, far stronger than a documentation search. PR must be owned by our application. Client PDF classification of PR as Zoho ERP Standard refers to the product feature, not an API.

findings.title: The GRN leg of line-level matching is broken; the PO-to-bill leg is intact
findings.impact: PO line to BILL line IS linked via purchaseorder_item_id on the bill line, so commitment-to-actual conversion and double-count prevention are achievable against documented fields. PO line to RECEIPT line is NOT linked: receipt lines expose no purchaseorder_item_id and no project/tag/custom-field coding, and the module has no list or search endpoint. Consequence: received-but-unbilled exposure and partial-GRN tracking cannot be derived from Zoho alone and must be reconstructed in our application or raised as an open question to Zoho.
findings.correction_note: Supersedes an earlier, over-broad statement that line-level matching could not be completed at all. The commitment-to-actual leg DOES work.

findings.title: Purchase Order LINE items do carry project_id, tags, item_custom_fields, account_id and location_id
findings.impact: POSITIVE. CAPEX code, WBS code and budget head can be carried at PO line level via project_id, reporting tags and item_custom_fields. This is the enabling fact for line-level commitment control.

findings.title: Zoho ERP Projects are flat; hierarchy exists only under Tasks via parent_id
findings.impact: REFUTES the earlier page-scraped claim that ERP Projects offer only two levels with no parent field. Tasks do expose parent_id, so nesting is possible under a project. However Project carries only scalar budget fields (budget_amount, budget_type, cost_budget_amount) with no budget-by-head object, so the multi-level WBS and budget register must remain owned by our application.

findings.title: There is no API to CREATE a custom field definition; only to set values on a record
findings.impact: The CAPEX/WBS custom-field layout cannot be provisioned as code. It must be created manually in the Zoho ERP UI per organisation, then discovered by the connector. This becomes a documented manual prerequisite in the setup wizard and the handover section.

findings.title: The published OAuth scope list covers a small fraction of the real scope surface
findings.impact: Least-privilege scope design must be driven from the specification, not the OAuth documentation page. Closes the gap flagged by lane R10.

findings.title: Pagination contract is now evidenced
findings.impact: per_page default 200 with a documented maximum of 200; page defaults to 1. Closes the unevidenced pagination gap flagged by lane R10 and lets bulk-extract sizing be specified rather than probed.

findings.title: Fixed assets cannot be linked to a source project, PO or bill, and cannot be incrementally synced
findings.impact: Capitalisation cannot be traced from asset back to the CWIP that funded it using documented fields, and the asset list cannot be polled incrementally (no created_time / last_modified_time). Capitalisation reconciliation must be anchored on our own capitalisation-request record, and asset sync must be full-refresh.

findings.title: Journal and bill LINES carry project_id and tags; bill HEADER does not
findings.impact: POSITIVE for capitalisation: a CWIP-transfer journal can be WBS-coded at line level. Also means every WBS-to-transaction mapping must be defined at LINE level, never header — a binding rule for the field-mapping workbench.

findings.title: Vendor advances have no dedicated endpoint or flag
findings.impact: An advance is simply a vendor payment whose bills[] allocation array is empty. There is no is_advance flag, so classifying capital advances for budget-exposure purposes requires our own derivation rule.

corrections_log.what: OAS-03 was initially stated as a blanket failure of line-level matching. Verified against the specification: bill lines DO carry purchaseorder_item_id. Only the receipt leg lacks linkage. Severity reduced CRITICAL to HIGH and the finding split.
